body.statement: For the fixed \(\mathcal A\), when \(L=0\), the refinement class contains one finite static ADMG on \(V\), \(\operatorname{TID\text{-}SCG}(H,0,\mathcal A,X,Y,0,x,y)\) reduces to ordinary ID on the common product alphabet, \(F\) equals the ordinary ID functional on success, and \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{lag}}(\mathcal A)\) reduces to an ordinary query-specific hedge on failure.
body.justification: The static boundary is the required sanity reduction to the complete fixed-ADMG benchmark.
body.gap: This is a reduction check rather than a novelty claim.
body.consumer: Users recover standard ID behavior without a separate implementation when no temporal uncertainty is present.

obligation.what_is_open: The claims about the behavior and failure output of \(\operatorname{TID\text{-}SCG}\) when \(L=0\).
obligation.obstruction: At \(L=0\) the graph and query reduce to a static slice, but the current core still provides no algorithmic transition rules that can be shown to coincide with ordinary ID. The general stationary-lift lemma used for failure was also false on fixed alphabets and has been narrowed.
obligation.attempted: I reduced the structural graph and causal query to one static ADMG and checked ordinary-ID soundness. This proves the semantic boundary but not the asserted behavior of an undefined procedure or its certificate encoder.
obligation.partial_result: When \(L=0\), every allowed directed or bidirected edge lies within one time slice, and the lag-zero query is therefore the ordinary static query on the slice ADMG \(H\).  Ordinary ID is sound for this query.  The assertion that the presently undefined \(\operatorname{TID\text{-}SCG}\) procedure reduces to ID, and its fixed-alphabet stationary failure-certificate claim, do not follow until the normal form and a suitable negative lift are supplied.
